newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Centam nations eye more 2H '97 ACPC coffee quotas.
newsitem.headline: Centam nations eye more 2H '97 ACPC coffee quotas.

text.p: The full council of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) is likely to confirm on May 20 a motion to increase the export quotas of Costa Rica and El Salvador in the second half of 1997, a Costa Rican coffee official said Thursday.

Guillermo Canet told Reuters that both nations had requests approved at a March 20 technical meeting of the ACPC to be allocated an extra 200,000 60-kg bags of coffee exports in the upcoming cycle, making a total of 400,000 extra bags.
"The decision of the technical group, adopted March 20 in London, will have to be confirmed in the council meeting of the ACPC on May 20 in the same city," Canet said.

The export quota adjustments will be on top of the original quotas allocated at the June 1996 meeting of the ACPC in Bogota, Colombia, where the cartel's export quota scheme to control world bean flows was first unveiled.

"Our interest is to find a mechanism that allows us, Costa Rica and El Salvador, to escape from the situation of having a large quantity of accumulated coffee," Canet said, without detailing stock figures.
According to the Bogota accord, Costa Rica was to export a total of 2,267,000 60-kg bags between July 1 1996 and June 30, 1997. El Salvador's quota was 2,337,000 bags.
The bid for additional second half 1997 quotas is separate from a move to carve up 200,000 bags of new quotas between Costa Rica and El Salvador.

These 200,000 bags, which the ACPC approved at the March technical meeting, appertain to the first half of 1997, not the second half. Salvadoran coffee leaders said seperately Thursday that both nations would share the 200,000 bag allotment.
